topic: How can frequency planning address interference between satellite uplinks and broadband power line communication systems?
response: Frequency planning can address interference between satellite uplinks and broadband power line communication systems by allocating non-overlapping frequency bands. The downlink frequency range for C-band is 3.7-4.2 GHz, which overlaps with the frequency range of broadband power line communication systems (typically in the range of 10-40 MHz). To mitigate this interference, satellite operators can use orthogonal polarizations or divide the frequency band into sub-bands.
reference_context: The context mentions various frequency bands for satellite communications, including C-band (downlink: 3.7-4.2 GHz), Ku-band (uplink: 14.0-14.5 GHz, downlink: 12.5-12.75 GHz), Ka-band (uplink: 27.5-31.0 GHz, downlink: 17.7-19.7 GHz), and others.
